Area.evidence_source: His daughter performs a speech act that is both a directive, in that the intention appears to have been to get her father to intervene with the police, and a commissive, in that she directly communicates a threat to take her life.Father responds to the directive element by offering reassurance and justifies non-intervention.Because it is uttered while intoxicated, the father questions the sincerity of the commissive element of the speech act.This interpretation was informed by an historic evidence base of similar situations in which his daughter had been intoxicated.Despite the doubt cast on the sincerity of the suicide speech act, the perlocutionary effect is as intended. The message is communicated emotionally and causes father to consider possible interventions to support his daughter. However, the situational context of the SCE (his fatigued state) tips the balance towards deciding against active intervention.In his narrative evaluation, the father reflects on the consequences of questioning the sincerity of utterances made while intoxicated. The story is presented as a moral tale to warn others that, whatever the circumstances, the mention of suicide indicates the presence of suicidal ideation, which may sooner or later result in a suicidal act.
